poster_title: Revisiting Hallucination Detection with Effective Rank-based Uncertainty
authors: Rui Wang, Zeming Wei, Guanzhang Yue, Meng Sun (Peking University)

content: LLMs have transformed generative and reasoning tasks.
Hallucinations pose a significant challenge for trustworthy deployment.
Current detection methods are impractical for real-time applications.
Existing UQ methods are computationally impractical.
Need for lightweight, self-contained, and scalable UQ techniques.
Current methods often rely on external tools or costly annotations.
Propose using effective rank of hidden states as a measure of uncertainty.
Effective rank captures semantic variations without additional knowledge.
Validated on multiple benchmark datasets and model architectures.
Effective rank outperforms or matches strong baselines.
Method is efficient and scalable for real-time applications.
Method effectively detects hallucinations and generalizes robustly.
Further research needed to explore internal-external semantic relationship.
